extracted.intended_audience: poets, poetry students, and readers interested in poetic craft and criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and critical standards for composing and evaluating narrative ballads and lyrical odes (characterization, metre, diction, thematic consistency, and the use of repetition), as discussed in the poet's explanatory notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Represent a picture consistent with the speaker's character
rubrics_metrics.description: "first, to represent a picture which should not be unimpressive yet consistent with the character that should describe it"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select a speaker/character whose manner of description plausibly fits the imagery and tone. Example given: a retired captain (past middle age, credulous and talkative) is chosen so the poem's supernatural material is credible coming from him.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure the speaker's passionate words convey passion to readers
rubrics_metrics.description: "while I adhered to the style in which such persons describe, to take care that words, which in their minds are impregnated with passion, should likewise convey passion to Readers who are not accustomed to sympathize with men feeling in that manner or using such language."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use language that, though natural to the character, is charged enough to communicate feeling to readers unfamiliar with that temperament; weighing words by feeling is essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use metre to shape perceived pace (lyrical and rapid metre)
rubrics_metrics.description: "It seemed to me that the Poem, to be natural, should in reality move slowly; yet I hoped, that, by the aid of the metre, to those who should at all enter into the spirit of the Poem, it would appear to move quickly."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a subject or speaker requires a slow, natural movement, employ lyrical/rapid metre to create the impression of momentum; metre can counterbalance narrative slowness and engage readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choose character traits that plausibly produce the poem's effects (superstition example)
rubrics_metrics.description: The author selects a character type (e.g., 'a Captain of a small trading vessel... past the middle age... retired... credulous and talkative... prone to superstition').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Build characters with psychological traits (slow faculties, deep feelings, adhesive minds) that justify their speech, beliefs, and the poem's thematic developments; this aids verisimilitude when exploring phenomena like superstition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish imagination from fancy in poetic invention
rubrics_metrics.description: "Superstitious men... have a reasonable share of imagination, by which word I mean the faculty which produces impressive effects out of simple elements; but they are utterly destitute of fancy, the power by which pleasure and surprize are excited by sudden varieties of situation and by accumulated imagery."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer imaginative synthesis (creating powerful effects from simple materials) over mere fancy (showy, sudden variety). Know which faculty you are invoking to produce the poem's effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Weigh words by feeling; purposeful repetition is a stylistic device
rubrics_metrics.description: "Words, a Poet's words more particularly, ought to be weighed in the balance of feeling and not measured by the space which they occupy upon paper... There are also various other reasons why repetition and apparent tautology are frequently beauties of the highest kind."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not avoid repetition merely from fear of tautology; repeated words can intensify passion and be aesthetically valuable if motivated by feeling. Choose diction for emotional weight, not economy alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry should be grounded in genuine passion; accept language's inadequacy
rubrics_metrics.description: "Poetry is passion: it is the history or science of feelings: now every man must know that an attempt is rarely made to communicate impassioned feelings without something of an accompanying consciousness of the inadequateness of our own powers, or the deficiencies of language."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authentic emotional investment is central; do not expect diction to fully contain feeling—acknowledge and use the strain between passion and linguistic limits as part of poetic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ode requirements: strong transitions and impassioned versification
rubrics_metrics.description: "[On Revisiting the Wye] ...it was written with a hope that in the transitions, and the impassioned music of the versification would be found the principal requisites of that species of composition."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For ode-like poems, prioritize fluid, meaningful transitions and musical, impassioned versification as defining structural and sonic features.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide an introductory/fram­ing piece if necessary for full effect
rubrics_metrics.description: "This Poem ought to have been preceded by an introductory Poem... an introductory Poem is necessary to give this Poem its full effect."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider prefatory material or framing poems to prepare readers for a poem's tonal or narrative demands; lack of an introduction can lessen impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal character must have a distinct, believable character
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique: "the principal person has no distinct character, either in his profession of Mariner, or as a human being..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid protagonists who lack clear personal identity or believable occupation-based behaviors; distinct characterization is essential for reader engagement and credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protagonist should act rather than be merely acted upon
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique: "he does not act, but is continually acted upon"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Give the protagonist agency; readers expect the central figure to make choices or incite events rather than be a passive vessel of happenings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure events have necessary causal/structural connections
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique: "the events having no necessary connection do not produce each other"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Structure narrative so that incidents follow from one another plausibly; avoid sequences of unconnected episodes that undermine coherence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-laborious accumulation of imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Critique: "the imagery is somewhat too laboriously accumulated."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be careful not to overload the poem with dense or excessive imagery; judicious, well-placed images often have greater effect than continual accumulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Versification should be harmonious and artfully varied within metre
rubrics_metrics.description: "the versification... is harmonious and artfully varied, exhibiting the utmost powers of that metre, and every variety of which it is capable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work within metrical constraints to produce variety and harmony in sound and rhythm; skilful variation of metre and verse forms strengthens poetic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genuine passion, felicitous images, and polished language are highest merits
rubrics_metrics.description: "the passion is every where true to nature; a great number of the stanzas present beautiful images, and are expressed with unusual felicity of language..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for authentic emotional truth, well-crafted imagery, and felicitous diction—these qualities can outweigh formal or structural shortcomings in a poem.
